To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) Generative and discriminative models differ in the way they learn the parameters of the successive layers, with more independence between layers in generative models; (ii) This difference is related to the fact that generative models are more robust to the order of the training data.
the weights of successive convolutional layer in deep generative models are more independent than in discriminative models, which results in improved performance.

the independence of successive convolutional layer kernels is a good indicator for a good generative model, and that the independence is higher in the generative process compared to the extraction of information from data.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of what makes the process of building patterns different from extracting them, and we provide an analysis that is both theoretically sound and empirically validated.
the question of what makes a good generator and how it is related to the task of information extraction from data.
the question whether the process of learning the parameters of the two architectures is the same.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
\textit{generative models are better than discriminative models}.

the generative architecture is more efficient than the extraction one in terms of the independence of successive layers, but the extraction one is more efficient in terms of the final quality of generated images.
the generative architecture of deep convolutional networks learns more independent patterns than the discriminative architecture.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
building a pattern is easier than extracting it.

, when building a generative model, the parameters of the successive layers of the model should be less dependent on each other, whereas, when extracting patterns from data, the parameters of these layers should be more dependent on each other.
building patterns is easier than extracting patterns from data.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the two deep architectures are not equivalent and that the independence of mechanisms principle can be used to better understand and improve the performance of these architectures.

the two architectures are not just mirror images of each other, and that the differences in the dependencies between successive layers can be used as a diagnostic tool for the performance of the architectures.
the same architecture can be used in two different settings: building and extracting a pattern from data.
